## Brief
Write `tests/test_hooks_projects.py`: the hook tests of cross-repository projects, from docs/design/2026-09-14-cross-repository-projects.md §3.2 (the path table), §6.1 (session mode), §6.2 (each hook), §6.4 (failure policy) and the `test_hooks_projects.py` bullets of §7.3. You write the tests against the spec while your parent (Sebago) builds the code in bin/spud_ledger.py; your tests are expected to be red until his phase B lands. Your only deliverable is that one file; tests/helpers.py and everything else are his.

Eric's answers override the design wherever it assumed otherwise:
1. `project add` defaults to `--sessions claim`; the home project stays `always`.
2. The stand-in for BadTakes is key `badtakes`, ticket prefix `BAD`, team prefix `BADS` (so tickets `BAD-001`, teams `BADS-001`, descriptions `BADS-001/<Name> (01, scout)`). Never TAKE/TAKES.

Interfaces your parent commits to (write against these exactly):
- `spud --as spud project add <path> --key badtakes --ticket-prefix BAD --team-prefix BADS --landing pr [--sessions claim|always]` (the path must be a git main checkout; resolve tempdirs with Path.resolve(), /var is /private/var).
- `spud --as spud ticket new --project badtakes --title ... --status active` gives BAD-001 / BADS-001.
- `spud --as spud member new --ticket BAD-001 --persona scout --model haiku --brief ... --deliverable 'src/**' --deliverable 'spud:docs/x.md'` (a `<key>:<glob>` qualifier names another project's checkout).
- `spud --as spud session claim [--project <key>]` needs `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` in its environment and records a claim for that session id; `session release` ends it.
- `spud hook <Event> [--project <key>]`. The hook reads `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` from its own process environment (the session's launch directory), falling back to the payload's `cwd`. Mode: `outside` (maps to no project; behaves as spud), `spud` (a claim for the payload's session_id, or the launch project's sessions is `always`), `plain` otherwise.
- Refusal needles you may assert (substring): a Spud session (no agent_id) writing a path in a badtakes checkout: "Law 1". A member writing outside its globs: "Law 5". A plain session or an unbound agent_id of a plain session writing any home path: "not Spud". An unbound agent_id in a Spud session writing a project path: "not bound". The state dir `.spud/` at any project root: "ledger database" for everyone. Home `ledger/**`/`reports/**`: "Law 5" for everyone. A plain session's Bash `spud --as spud ticket new ...`: "Law 6" and "/spud"; its `spud --as spud session claim` is allowed (decision allow, since it is a vouched spud call through the home's own launcher: copy bin/spud into the scratch home as HookCase.setUp does).
- SessionStart: a plain session gets `additionalContext` of one line, at most 300 bytes (UTF-8), containing "/spud" and the project key; an `always` project's unclaimed session gets a line containing "run /spud now"; a claimed session in badtakes gets at most 2048 bytes naming `badtakes` and containing "you are Spud here"; a home session gets the board as today ("Ledger board").
- Plain session: PreToolUse(Agent) for an ordinary spawn (subagent_type e.g. "general-purpose", a free description, even `isolation: "worktree"`) is silent (no stdout) and writes no spawn_requests row; a spudagent-shaped spawn (subagent_type `spudagent`, or a description matching `BADS-001/Name (01, scout)`) gets the full check and is denied. PostToolUse(Agent) with no spawn_requests row writes no hook.error. SubagentStart and SubagentStop for an unbound agent write no event and print nothing. Stop is silent even with a sessionless planned member older than ten minutes (set its planned_at back directly in the scratch database, as tests/test_hooks.py StopSessionTest does).
- §6.4: with the scratch database made unreadable (see FailurePolicyTest.break_database in tests/test_hooks.py), `spud hook PreToolUse --project badtakes` exits 2 for a payload carrying agent_id and exits 0 with no decision for one without; without `--project` it stays exit 2 for both.
- A `BADS-001/Name (01, scout)` description binds exactly like `SPUD-nnn` (PreToolUse allow, PostToolUse binds, member active).

Build: subclass or reuse `HookCase`/`SpudTestCase` from tests/test_hooks.py and tests/helpers.py by import (do not edit them). Build the other repository in setUp with subprocess git and a clean environment, the way `WorktreeElsewhereTest` does (tests/test_hooks.py around line 2883): `git init -b main`, an empty commit, `git worktree add` for a worktree case. Keep your runner helpers (a CLI run with a given cwd and env, a hook run with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set) inside your file. Pop `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` from any env you copy from os.environ unless the test sets it. Cover every cell of the §3.2 table through PreToolUse(Write) and through a Bash redirect (`echo x > <path>`), for: Spud session, plain session, bound member of BAD-001 (globs above), unbound agent_id in a Spud session, unbound agent_id in a plain session; targets in the badtakes root, in a badtakes worktree, in the home (SPUD_PATHS file like CLAUDE.md, another home path like bin/x, ledger/x.md), `.spud/` at the badtakes root, and outside every project. Use subTest for the matrix.

Verify: the file imports and is collected (`python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests -p test_hooks_projects.py`), and every failure today is the missing feature (argparse rejecting `project`/`session`/`--project`, or the old behaviour), not a bug in your helpers. Never run bin/spud without SPUD_HOME pointing at a scratch home; never touch /Users/ericlugo/Personal/Spud or /Users/ericlugo/Personal/BadTakes outside this worktree's tests/test_hooks_projects.py.
